text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Government seeks to keep its course on budget, while finance ministry sources hint at a deficit near 3.4 to 3.5 percent of GDP, the government expects an improvement of tax revenues and studies savings.
-- Unions criticise Prime Minister Lionel Jospin for not being able to prevent a shutdown of the Renault car assembly plant in Vilvoorde, Belgium.
-- Guinness and GrandMet executives to meet LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault on Wednesday about his opposition to their merger plans.
-- Jospin driven to cutting public deficits in 1997.
-- A reform of SNCF railway authority, questioned by transports ministry, to be maintained.
-- Italian insurer Generali to strengthen its position in France.
-- Subscriber TV-channel Canal Plus negotiates with Germany's Leo Kirch and Bertelsmann on the sale of its 37.5 percent stake in Premiere channel.
-- Belgian Prime Minister criticises Jospin for letting people hope he could cancel the planned shutdown of the Renault Vilvoorde plant.
-- Pernod Ricard chairman says in an interview the beverage group is not seeking an alliance, adds there are currently few opportunities to buy in its sector.
-- Shutdown of Renault plant at Vilvoorde could not be prevented by cuts in working hours, according to the mediator in charge of studying possible alternatives to the shutdown.
